findings.claim: The fix guards the remainder with `if rest and any(rest)`, which drops any nonempty remainder whose elements are all falsey (e.g. [0], [None], [False], [0, 0]). The requirement only asks to suppress an empty trailing group and to preserve a nonempty remainder.
findings.impact: split_after([1, 0], lambda x: x == 1, maxsplit=1) yields [[1]] instead of [[1], [0]], silently losing data. The independent report's diagnostic profile seeded_falsey_remainder_v1 fails 4 of 6 cases (zero, none, false, zeros), confirming the regression.

findings.claim: The independent report shows accepted_against_baseline=false and status=failed: issue checks 10/10 and targeted 4/4 pass, but the disclosed diagnostic checks fail (2/6) and full_suite_all_passed is false (659/660).
findings.impact: Acceptance against baseline is not met. Note the remaining full-suite failure test_more.TimeLimitedTests.test_zero_limit is a pre-existing baseline failure (baseline_failures count 1, new_failures count 0), so it is not caused by this change; however the diagnostic falsey-remainder failures are attributable to the candidate's `any(rest)` guard.

unknowns: Whether the intended fix should be simply `if rest:` (dropping only the empty list) rather than any falsey check
Whether additional split_after call sites or docs/tests elsewhere assume the old behavior
